newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Japan emperor unveils friendship statue in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Japan emperor unveils friendship statue in Brazil.

text.p: Japan's Emperor Akihito and Empress Michiko Friday wrapped up their visit to Sao Paulo by unveiling a statue commemorating the 100th anniversary of a friendship treaty between the two countries.
Most of the 1.3 million Brazilians of Japanese descent live in Brazil's sprawling industrial capital and the city houses the largest Japanese community abroad.
Akihito also visited the University of Sao Paulo, where he met elite students and professors in fields related to his own area of expertise, marine biology and ichthyology, the study of fish.
He gave the university a copy of his own book on Japanese fish, which covers 200 species.
The emperor and empress, nearing the end of a 10-day tour of Brazil, were due to visit a retirement home for Japanese-Brazilians before leaving by plane for Curitiba, the capital of Parana state.

Their two-day tour of Sao Paulo included a visit to the city's Japanese neighbourhood of Liberdade and to Morumbi stadium where thousands of delirious fans gathered for the final of the state soccer championship Thursday.
Akihito and Michiko, making the first Japanese imperial visit to Latin America, will fly to Buenos Aires on Monday for a three-day visit to Argentina.
